introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education Board, General Certificate of Education Examination, 0550 Geography 1, June 2023, Ordinary Level. Multiple choice question paper, one and a half hours. Answer ALL the 50 questions. Calculators are allowed. Each question has FOUR suggested answers: A, B, C and D. Mark only one answer for each question; if you mark more than one answer you score zero for that question. Avoid spending too much time on any one question.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D. Questions 1-6 use the topographic map in Fig. 1, question 13 uses the climograph in Fig. 2, questions 14-15 are pairs of statements, question 45 uses the map of Cameroon in Fig. 3.

figures.legende: Hand-drawn topographic map extract (Fig. 1, untitled): grid with eastings 00-03 and northings 11-15, closed 800 m contour in square 0014, contours 700, 600, 500 and 400 m, a thick river flowing south, a church and buildings near the top, a Trig Station on the left, key and north arrow (Questions 1-6).
Hand-drawn climograph (Fig. 2): monthly rainfall bars J to D with maxima in June-July and October, a nearly flat temperature line, total 2920 mm and temperature range 3.2 °C (Question 13).
Hand-drawn outline map of Cameroon with a northern zone marked I and the hatched southern zone marked II (Question 45).

incertitudes: Page de garde verifiee : « GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD », 0550 GEOGRAPHY 1, JUNE 2023, ORDINARY LEVEL, Multiple Choice Question Paper, One and a half hours, « Answer ALL the 50 questions », calculatrices permises. Le sujet n'imprime aucune cle ni aucun bareme.

Aucun corrige officiel : toutes les reponses sont deduites par le redacteur (aucune cle imprimee). Les calculs (intervalle vertical 100 m, coordonnees 016145 contre 003131, grand cercle 120 + 60 = 180, regle de 1 °C pour 165 m soit environ 6,06 °C pour 1000 m) ont ete recalcules avec Python.

Fig. 1 (Q1-6) : carte topographique dessinee a la main, sans titre ni echelle (comme l'indique le sujet), lue sur la page : courbes 400 a 800 m, equidistance 100 m, carre 0014 = easting 00, northing 14 (contour ferme 800). Les etiquettes de la grille en bas a gauche (« 00 », « 11 ») sont partiellement illisibles ; sans effet sur les reponses. Une petite marque parasite precede l'option B de la Q1 sur le scan ; ignoree.

Q4 : question defectueuse (une altitude de 700 m n'est pas une pente, les options decrivent la pente, pas d'echelle). Convertie en question ouverte ; reponse visee « Gentle » (courbes 700/600 assez espacees) donnee comme lecture la plus probable, non certaine.

Q6 : deux options correctes (le village est sur la rive est du cours d'eau, qui coule vers le sud : rive gauche = rive est, options B et D). Convertie en question ouverte ; reponse visee B (Left Bank), qui est aussi la rive est.
Q27 : options B et C imprimees identiques (« i, ii, iv. »), et c'est la bonne combinaison. Convertie en question ouverte ; reponse visee i, ii, iv.

Q29 : l'enonce mele des traits des stades 3 (take-off : croissance rapide des industries) et 4 (drive to maturity : investissements elargis, niveau de vie). Convertie en question ouverte ; reponse visee stade 4, a confirmer.

Q47 : options B (tropical continental) et C (North East Trade) decrivent le meme air sec venu du nord ; A et D de meme pour l'air maritime. Convertie en question ouverte ; reponse visee C (North East Trade, harmattan).

Fig. 2 (Q13) : climographe dessine a la main, sans axes gradues, lu ainsi : total 2920 mm, ecart de temperature 3,2 °C, mois les plus secs en debut d'annee, maxima en juin-juillet et en octobre. Reponse retenue D (Equatorial), cle non imprimee ; Tropical Monsoon est l'alternative ecartee.

Cles non imprimees, choix argumentes mais dependants de l'intention des examinateurs : Q8 (la rotation est retenue comme non-cause ; l'option D est plutot une consequence de l'inclinaison), Q12 (« isolines » est le terme general, « isohyets » le terme specifique retenu), Q14 (6 °C par 1000 m retenu comme vrai : environ 6,06 °C par la regle de 1 °C pour 165 m ; 6,5 °C est la valeur moyenne usuelle), Q18, Q26 (dormant retenu plutot qu'extinct), Q36, Q39 (A retenu, D en est une formulation vague), Q48 (« human problem » interprete comme main-d'oeuvre non qualifiee).

Q38 : le libelle de l'option C (« Economic and monetary union of central African states ») s'ecarte de l'intitule officiel (Communaute economique et monetaire de l'Afrique centrale) mais reste la seule option correcte. Q46 : l'orthographe imprimee « Mini Matarpe » est conservee ; le corrige ne s'appuie pas sur ce nom.

Q45 (Fig. 3) : fond de carte du Cameroun dessine a la main, zones I et II, lettres A, B, R, X, Y, Z sans legende ; le corrige lit la zone II hachuree comme le sud forestier du pays (foret dense equatoriale), non confirme par une legende imprimee.

Figures : trois PNG recadres depuis la numerisation (regime « B_cuit », page rendue avec filtre de niveaux, controle OCR OK, aucun filigrane lisible) ; les dessins originaux, faits a la main, restent grossiers.
Q43 : « Mining » est cite parmi les « services » imprimes ; le corrige lit la liste comme des activites et retient « Manufacturing » comme exception.
Converties en questions ouvertes par le relecteur (clé ou options discutables) : 4, 6, 27, 29, 47. Voir les incertitudes detaillees ci-dessus.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Study the topographic map extract (Fig. 1, untitled) and answer questions 1-6.

![fig-1](gce-ol-geography-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

**1.** State the approximate height of the land in square 0014.
questions.corrige_markdown: In a four-figure grid reference the first two figures are the easting and the last two the northing of the lower-left corner of the square. Square 0014 is the square between eastings 00 and 01 and between northings 14 and 15, at the top left of the map. It contains a closed contour labelled 800, so the land there is at about 800 m above sea level. Options C and D use the wrong units (centimetres and kilometres, which would be absurd heights), and the 700 m contour does not pass through this square. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Use the map in Fig. 1 (see question 1).

![fig-1](gce-ol-geography-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

**2.** To what direction will one travel to the church (016145) from Trig Station (003131)?
questions.corrige_markdown: Read each six-figure reference as easting (first three figures) then northing (last three). The Trig Station 003131 is at easting 00.3 and northing 13.1. The church 016145 is at easting 01.6 and northing 14.5. The church is 1.3 grid units further east and 1.4 grid units further north, so one must travel north east. On the map the church is indeed in the upper middle part, up and to the right of the triangle that marks the Trig Station. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Use the map in Fig. 1 (see question 1).

![fig-1](gce-ol-geography-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

**3.** Calculate the Vertical Interval (VI) of the above sketch.
questions.corrige_markdown: The vertical interval is the difference in height between two successive contours. The contours on the sketch are labelled 400, 500, 600, 700 and 800 m, so $VI = 500 - 400 = 100\ \text{m}$ (the same between every pair of neighbouring contours). Height is measured in metres here, so options B and C are wrong, and 400 m is the lowest labelled contour, not the interval. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Use the map in Fig. 1 (see question 1).

![fig-1](gce-ol-geography-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

**4.** The landscape 700m above sea level (asl) can be described as:

*Options as printed:* A) Gentle.   B) Steep.   C) Level.   D) Flat.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The words in the options describe the slope of the land, which on a contour map is shown by how close together the contour lines are: widely spaced contours mean a gentle slope, closely packed contours a steep slope, and no contours at all a level or flat surface. A height of 700 m above sea level says nothing about slope by itself, and the sketch has no scale, so the gradient cannot be calculated. On the sketch the 700 m and 600 m contours are fairly far apart, and the land is not flat or level because it falls from 800 m to 400 m across the map; the most likely intended answer is therefore Gentle. Because the question mixes height and slope, it is best treated as an open question: explain that the land at 700 m is hilly upland and that the spacing of contours shows a moderate to gentle slope.

**Intended answer: A (Gentle).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

The church gives the settlement a religious function and the group of buildings, which are houses, gives it a residential function. Nothing on the map (no railway or road station, hotel, government office or farm symbol) supports transport, tourism, administrative or farming functions. **Answer: B.**

**6.** The site of the village is on the River's:

*Options as printed:* A) Right Bank;   B) Left Bank;   C) Western Bank;   D) Eastern Bank.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The village (buildings and church) is drawn on the east side of the thick river line. The river flows from the north, near the village, towards the south (the contours show the land falling towards the bottom of the map). The left and right banks are named by looking downstream, so for a river flowing south the left bank is the east side. The village is therefore on the Left Bank, which is also the Eastern Bank. Options B and D are both correct descriptions, so the question cannot be marked as a single-choice item and is left open: a full answer is 'on the left bank (the east bank) of the river'.

**Intended answer: B (Left Bank;).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: **7.** A traveller crossing the International Dateline from America to Asia on Sunday 9a.m would have to reset his watch to:
questions.corrige_markdown: The International Date Line (about 180 degrees longitude) lies in the Pacific. A traveller going from America (east of the line) to Asia (west of the line) moves westwards across it, and the calendar date is put forward by one day while the clock time stays the same. Sunday 9 a.m. becomes Monday 9 a.m. A traveller going the other way (Asia to America) would put the date back by one day. Saturday would be correct only for that opposite direction. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **8.** Identify the item below that is **not** a correct cause of seasons.
questions.corrige_markdown: Seasons result from the revolution of the Earth round the Sun in one year, combined with the tilt of its axis (about 23.5 degrees), which stays pointing in the same direction. Because of this, the tilt faces the Sun differently at different positions on the orbit, so the amount of energy (insolation) received by a hemisphere changes through the year. The rotation of the Earth on its axis takes about 24 hours and causes day and night, not seasons. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Energy Earth receives at different position.

questions.enonce_markdown: **9.** Identify the pair of longitudes that forms a great circle.
questions.corrige_markdown: A great circle divides the Earth into two equal halves. Two meridians form a great circle when they are on opposite sides of the Earth, that is when they are 180 degrees apart. 120° East and 60° West are on opposite sides: $120 + 60 = 180$. The other pairs are only $145 - 35 = 110$, $120 - 60 = 60$ and $120 - 60 = 60$ degrees apart, so they are not opposite meridians. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **10.** A dendritic drainage pattern is characterised by the flowing of:
questions.corrige_markdown: The word dendritic comes from the Greek word for tree: the main river is the trunk and the tributaries join it like branches, at acute angles, usually on uniform rock. Option A describes a parallel pattern, option C a radial pattern (streams flowing outward from a dome or highland) and option D a trellis or rectangular pattern. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Two or more streams adjacent to each other.
Streams in a tree like manner.
A stream out of a dome or highland.
Streams that connect to each other at right angle.

questions.enonce_markdown: **11.** The process by which water moves downward and vertically into the soil is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Infiltration is the entry of water from the surface into the soil. Percolation is the later, slower movement of water down through the soil and rock layers below. Throughflow is the lateral (sideways) movement of water in the soil towards a river, and base flow is the groundwater feeding a river. The process described, water entering the soil from above, is infiltration. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **12.** Places with the same amount of rainfall are joined by lines called:
questions.corrige_markdown: Isohyets are lines joining places of equal rainfall. Isobars join places of equal atmospheric pressure and isotherms join places of equal temperature. 'Isoline' is the general name for any line of equal value (the other three are particular kinds of isoline), so the specific term for rainfall, isohyet, is the answer. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Study the climograph in Fig. 2 and answer question 13.

![fig-2](gce-ol-geography-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.png)

**13.** The Climograph in Fig.2 is for?
questions.corrige_markdown: The climograph shows a very small annual temperature range of 3.2 °C and a high annual rainfall total of 2920 mm. Rain falls in nearly every month, with the driest months at the start of the year, and the bars show two maxima (a main one in June-July and a smaller one around October) separated by a dip, which is the double rainfall peak typical of an equatorial climate. Mediterranean climate would have a winter rainfall maximum and a dry summer, tropical continental has a long dry season and a larger temperature range, and tropical monsoon has a single, very wet summer peak and a clearly larger temperature range. The best match is Equatorial. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Instructions for questions 14-15.** Read the two statements. Determine if they are true or false. Then select as follows:

- **A** If both statements are true.
- **B** If the 1st is true and the 2nd is false.
- **C** If both statements are false.
- **D** If the 1st statement is false and 2nd is true.

**14.**

| First statement | Second statement |
|---|---|
| Temperature drops by 6 °C for every 1000m of ascent. | The larger the surface area covered by a given amount of insolation the more concentrated the energy. |
questions.corrige_markdown: First statement: in the troposphere the temperature falls with height at about 6 °C per 1000 m (the often-quoted rule of 1 °C for every 165 m gives $1000 / 165 \approx 6.06$ °C), so it is true. Second statement: when a given amount of insolation is spread over a larger surface area, the energy is more spread out (less concentrated), not more concentrated, so it is false. True then false is option B. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: The 1st is true and the 2nd is false.
The 1st statement is false and 2nd is true.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Instructions for questions 14-15** (see question 14): choose A if both statements are true, B if the 1st is true and the 2nd is false, C if both are false, D if the 1st is false and the 2nd is true.

**15.**

| First statement | Second statement |
|---|---|
| Moving air hits the vane, forcing the instrument's arrow to point a direction. | The instrument mentioned is the wind vane. |
questions.corrige_markdown: A wind vane is turned by the moving air so that its arrow points into the direction from which the wind blows, so the first statement is true. The instrument that has a vane and an arrow is the wind vane, so the second statement is true as well. Both are true: option A. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: The 1st is true and the 2nd is false.
The 1st statement is false and 2nd is true.

questions.enonce_markdown: **16.** Climate is different from weather in that:
questions.corrige_markdown: Weather is the state of the atmosphere of a place at a given moment or over a short time (a day, a week). Climate is the average weather of a place recorded over a long period, usually about 30 years or more. Options A and B describe weather, and D is not specific to climate because weather also involves temperature and rainfall. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: The real weather condition of a place is studied.
The weather condition is studied for a short time.
The average weather condition is studied for a long time.
The condition of temperature and rainfall of a place are studied.

questions.enonce_markdown: **17.** Trees of tropical Rain forest and coniferous forest are similar in that:
questions.corrige_markdown: Both forests are evergreen: the trees are never completely bare because they shed their leaves a few at a time all through the year. Tropical rainforest trees are tall hardwoods, whereas conifers have softwood. Conifer branches slope downward so that snow slides off, but this is not true of rainforest trees. Neither forest loses its leaves at one time (that is deciduous behaviour). **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: They lose their leaves at the same time.

questions.enonce_markdown: **18.** The most numerous members of a Trophic level in a food chain are:
questions.corrige_markdown: Energy is lost at each step of a food chain, so the lowest trophic level, the producers (green plants), has the largest number of organisms and each higher level has fewer. Herbivores, carnivores and omnivores come at higher levels and are less numerous. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **19.** The role of Decomposers in a food chain is to:
questions.corrige_markdown: Decomposers (bacteria and fungi) feed on dead plants and animals and their wastes and break them down, returning nutrients to the soil. Converting solar energy is done by producers through photosynthesis. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **20.** Rocks whose form is changed as a result of internal heat and pressure are named:
questions.corrige_markdown: Metamorphic rocks are existing rocks that have been changed (for example limestone into marble, or shale into slate) by great heat and pressure inside the Earth, without melting. Sedimentary rocks form from deposited material, and volcanic and plutonic rocks are igneous rocks that form from cooling magma on or below the surface. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **21.** Which one of the following combinations causes the increasing world demand for water?
questions.corrige_markdown: World demand for water rises because more people need water and because industry and irrigated, intensive farming use very large quantities of it. Fishing grounds are a use of the water body, not a use that takes water away, so options A, B and C that include them are wrong. Only D has two real causes: growth of industry and modern intensive farming. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Population growth and more fishing grounds.
More fishing ground and modern intensive farming.
Growth of industry and more fishing grounds.
Growth of industry and modern intensive farming.

questions.enonce_markdown: **22.** The buttress roots of trees of the tropical rainforest are useful in that they:
questions.corrige_markdown: Many tropical rainforest trees are very tall but have shallow root systems because the nutrients are in the top soil. Buttress roots are large, wide, plank-like roots at the base of the trunk that spread the weight and give support to the tall tree. They do not stop people from felling trees and do not reach the water table. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Provide hide out for wild life,
Prevent the trees from being felled,

questions.enonce_markdown: **23.** The correct order of the Earth's structure from its interior is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Starting from the centre of the Earth and going outwards the layers are the inner core (solid), the outer core (liquid), the mantle and finally the thin crust. Options B, C and D put the layers in the wrong order. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Inner core, outer core, mantle, crust.
Outer core, inner core, crust, mantle.
Inner core, outer core, crust, mantle.
Mantle, crust, outer core, inner core.

questions.enonce_markdown: **24.** On which plate boundary are ocean trenches formed?
questions.corrige_markdown: Ocean trenches form at destructive (convergent) plate boundaries, where a denser oceanic plate is forced down under another plate in a subduction zone. Constructive boundaries are where plates move apart and new crust is formed (ocean ridges), and at conservative boundaries plates slide past each other. Collision zones, where two continental plates meet, make fold mountains rather than trenches. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **25.** Select from the following combinations the one that gives only processes of chemical weathering.
questions.corrige_markdown: Chemical weathering changes the minerals of rocks by chemical reactions: oxidation, hydrolysis, carbonation, hydration and solution. Exfoliation, frost shattering and pressure release are all physical (mechanical) weathering processes. Only B has two chemical processes. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **26.** Volcanoes that have not shown evidence of eruption for a long time are considered as:
questions.corrige_markdown: A dormant volcano is one that has not erupted for a long time but could erupt again. An active volcano erupts regularly or has erupted recently, and an extinct volcano is one that is not expected to erupt again. 'Passive' is not a standard class of volcano. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
**27.** Select three correct statements from the following on weathering and denudation.

- i) During weathering rocks are broken down by nature.
- ii) During Erosion rocks are worn down.
- iii) Weathering moves materials from one place to another.
- iv) Erosion includes the removal of loose materials.

*Options as printed:* A) i, ii, iii.   B) i, ii, iv.   C) i, ii, iv.   D) ii, iii, iv.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Statement i is true: weathering is the breakdown of rocks in place by natural agents. Statement ii is true: erosion wears the land down. Statement iv is true: erosion involves picking up and carrying away loose material. Statement iii is false: weathering takes place in situ and does not move the material, which is the work of erosion and transport. The three true statements are i, ii and iv. Options B and C are printed identically (both read 'i, ii, iv'), so a letter cannot be chosen fairly and the question is left open.

**Intended answer: B (i, ii, iv).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: **28.** Which one of the following is **not** an advantage of the informal sector to the economy?
questions.corrige_markdown: The informal sector creates jobs for people with few qualifications, recycles waste as raw material and sells cheap goods, which are all advantages. The involvement of many children (child labour) is a disadvantage and a social problem, so it is the item that is not an advantage. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Employment is created for low skilled workers.
Tends to use waste as raw material.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**29.** At what stage of Economic Development did WW Rostow (1960) place countries with the following characteristics: Rapid growth of industries, increased investments in agriculture/transport/services, and improved standard of living?

*Options as printed:* A) Stage 1 traditional society.   B) Stage 2 precondition for take off.   C) Stage 3 take off.   D) Stage 4 the drive to maturity.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Rostow's five stages are: 1 traditional society, 2 the preconditions for take-off, 3 take-off, 4 the drive to maturity and 5 the age of high mass consumption. Stage 1 has little industry, and stage 2 is only the preparation for growth. Rapid growth of industries is a feature of take-off (stage 3), but the other characteristics (investment spreading to agriculture, transport and services, a wider range of industries and a rising standard of living) fit the drive to maturity (stage 4) better. Because the list mixes features of stages 3 and 4, the question is left open; the best-supported answer is stage 4, the drive to maturity.

**Intended answer: D (Stage 4 the drive to maturity).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown:
**30.** The energy resource in the table with its correct classification is:

| | Energy Resource | Classification |
|---|---|---|
| A) | Natural Gas | Non-renewable |
| B) | Coal | Renewable |
| C) | HEP | Non-renewable |
| D) | Solar energy | Non renewable |
questions.corrige_markdown: Natural gas is a fossil fuel formed over millions of years and cannot be replaced at the rate it is used, so it is non-renewable. Coal is also non-renewable (not renewable), and hydro-electric power (HEP) and solar energy are renewable because water flow and sunlight are continuously renewed. Only row A is correct. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **31.** Another name for market gardening is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Market gardening is the intensive growing of vegetables, fruits and flowers on small plots, usually near towns, to sell in the market. It is also called truck farming. Horticulture is the wider science and art of growing garden plants, and crop farming and fruit farming are too general. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **32.** One natural reason why coniferous forest is easier to exploit is that:
questions.corrige_markdown: Coniferous trees grow in large groups of the same species (pure stands), so loggers do not have to search for the valuable species among many different kinds, and the wood is soft and straight. Equipment is not a natural reason, conifer forests often lie on hilly land, and the trees can be tall. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: The equipment used is very effective.
The trees are in pure stand.
The trees are not very tall.

questions.enonce_markdown: **33.** Identify the statement about Von Thunen's model of rural land use that is correct.
questions.corrige_markdown: In Von Thunen's model the locational (economic) rent of a piece of land is the profit that a farmer makes on it, equal to the market price of the crop minus the cost of production and the cost of transport to the market. The model assumes that all farmers get the same price at the market (so B is wrong), that their production costs are the same (so C is wrong), and that the intensity of production falls as the distance from the market increases (so D is wrong). **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: The profit from a piece of land is the locational rent.
Farmers get different prices for their crops.
Cost of production differed for all farmers.
Production increases with increasing distance from the market.

questions.enonce_markdown: **34.** Computers, lasers, space crafts, precision machines, telecom equipment are all products of:
questions.corrige_markdown: These goods are made with advanced technology, much research and highly skilled workers, which defines high-tech industries. Craft industries make hand-made goods in small workshops. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **35.** What other term can be used to mean non-renewable resources?
questions.corrige_markdown: Non-renewable resources (such as oil, coal and minerals) exist in a limited amount and cannot be replaced in a human lifetime, so they are also called finite resources. Infinite is the opposite and describes unlimited resources such as sunlight. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **36.** One major problem affecting tourist activities in LICs.
questions.corrige_markdown: Low-income countries (LICs) have little money, so governments invest little in tourism facilities such as roads, airports, hotels and security, which holds back tourism. Many LICs have rich tourist resources, so B is wrong, and a large number of visitors is a benefit, not a problem. Language barriers are a minor difficulty compared with the lack of investment. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **37.** The internet has the following weakness:
questions.corrige_markdown: A weakness is a disadvantage. Providing information for research, making new friends and advertising recreation sites are advantages of the internet. The risk of being scammed (cheated by online fraud) is a weakness. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: Raw materials for research is provided;

questions.enonce_markdown: **38.** The abbreviation CEMAC stands for:
questions.corrige_markdown: CEMAC is the Economic and Monetary Community of Central Africa (in French, Communaute Economique et Monetaire de l'Afrique Centrale). Of the printed options, C, 'Economic and monetary union of central African states', is the only one that has the economic and monetary parts and the central African states, so it is the best match. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Central economic members of African countries.
Economic and monetary union of central African states.
Economic union and movement of central African countries.

questions.enonce_markdown: **39.** In LEDCs railways were constructed mainly to:
questions.corrige_markdown: In most less economically developed countries (LEDCs) the railways were built in the colonial period as lines from the mines and farming areas of the interior to the coastal ports, to carry raw materials for export and to bring imported goods back to the interior. Options B and C are not the main purpose, and D is only a general statement: a railway links places on land, not countries overseas, so A is the precise answer. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Transport exports to the coast and imports to the interior.
Transport passengers to and fro the factories.
Facilitate the distribution of local produce.
Provide a link between the colonies and industrial countries (colonisers).

questions.enonce_markdown: **40.** A country having a population pyramid with a broad base and narrow apex shows that it experiences:
questions.corrige_markdown: A broad base means that there are many children, which comes from a high birth rate. The narrow apex means that few people reach old age, which shows a short life expectancy (and often a high death rate). Options B, C and D are the opposite of what the shape shows. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **41.** Which one of the following may **not** be considered as a function of urban settlements?
questions.corrige_markdown: Urban settlements have residential, cultural (libraries), recreational, commercial, administrative and other functions. Farming is the typical primary function of rural settlements, so it is not normally a function of a town. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **42.** Which of the following is NOT true of stage two of the Demographic Transition Development Model?
questions.corrige_markdown: In stage 2 the death rate falls because of better food, sanitation and control of disease, but the birth rate stays high, so the population grows fast. The infant mortality rate, although falling, is still high. The birth rate begins to fall only in stage 3, so 'falling birth rate' is not true of stage 2. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **43.** A rural settlement normally has the following services EXCEPT one. Which is the exception?
questions.corrige_markdown: The main activities of rural settlements are primary activities: farming, fishing and mining or quarrying. Manufacturing (making goods in factories) is a secondary activity that normally needs electricity, markets and many workers and is concentrated in towns, so it is the exception. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **44.** When two towns expand and eventually merge, they form a/an:
questions.corrige_markdown: A conurbation is a continuous urban area formed when neighbouring towns or cities grow outwards and join together. A millionaire city is simply a city of over one million people, and a megalopolis is a still larger chain of merged conurbations. Agglomeration is a general term for a cluster of urban activities or population. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Study the map of Cameroon in Fig. 3 and answer question 45.

![fig-3](gce-ol-geography-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_3.png)

**45.** The vegetation zone shaded II on the map of Cameroon above is good for lumbering because of:
questions.corrige_markdown: The shaded zone II covers the southern part of the country, which is the dense equatorial rainforest. Lumbering depends first of all on a rich supply of valuable timber trees, and the forest has many species (for example valuable hardwoods). The transport network, the climate and government policy help, but the main reason that makes the zone good for lumbering is the abundance of timber species. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **46.** The main factor favouring the development of the aluminium industry in the coastal industrial region of Cameroon is:
questions.corrige_markdown: Aluminium smelting uses a very large amount of electricity. The aluminium smelter of the coastal region is at Edea, which is supplied with cheap hydro-electric power (HEP) from dams on the Sanaga river, so HEP is the main favouring factor. Iron ore is not used to make aluminium, the bauxite deposits are far from the coast (in the interior of the country), and the local market and labour are not the main reason. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
**47.** The dominant wind blowing over Cameroon in December is:

*Options as printed:* A) Tropical maritime.   B) Tropical continental.   C) North East Trade.   D) Southwest Monsoon.
questions.corrige_markdown:
In December (the northern hemisphere winter) the Inter-Tropical Discontinuity lies far to the south, and the dry, dusty North East Trade winds (the Harmattan) blow from the Sahara over most of the country. The South West Monsoon (tropical maritime air from the Atlantic) dominates in the rainy season, from about March to October. Options B and C describe the same dry air from the north (a tropical continental air mass is the air carried by the North East Trade wind), and A and D likewise describe the same moist air from the south; the question is therefore left open, with 'North East Trade wind' as the answer expected.

**Intended answer: C (North East Trade).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: **48.** Select the main human problem of agriculture in Cameroon:
questions.corrige_markdown: Human problems are those that come from people, as opposed to physical problems (climate, soils, relief) and infrastructure. Most farmers use simple traditional methods, are not trained and are mostly unskilled, which keeps yields low. Poor transport and a small market are economic or infrastructure problems, and limited research is an institutional one. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **49.** The Economic union to which Cameroon is a top member is?
questions.corrige_markdown: Cameroon is a leading member of CEMAC, the Economic and Monetary Community of Central Africa. ECOWAS is the West African community that Cameroon does not belong to, UDEAC is the former customs union that CEMAC replaced, and ACP-EU is a partnership between countries of Africa, the Caribbean and Pacific and the European Union rather than an economic union of Central Africa. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: **50.** Name the drainage basin into which river Mungo flows.
questions.corrige_markdown: The Mungo rises in the highlands of western Cameroon and flows south to the Wouri estuary and the Gulf of Guinea, so it belongs to the Atlantic drainage basin. The Niger basin (Benue), the Lake Chad basin and the Congo basin (Sangha, Ngoko) drain other parts of the country. **Answer: D.**
